## CHAPTER TEN

## (PASSPORT PAINS)

● Because BEPO didn't take his traveling abroad seriously, he didn't renew

his passport when it expired two years ago.

● Bepo later settled for Ibadan to renew his passport due to crowd in Lagos

immigration offices. (Take note , The Nigeria Immigration service is in

charge of issuing / producing the international passport booklet).

● Bepo finally got in touch with an Agent who could help him get the

international passport faster. The agent named ‘TAI’ asked him to pay

N100, 000 for a 10 year renewal (64 pages) (Take note , the international

passport booklet has two categories; The 32 pages which is valid for 5

years & the 64 pages which is valid for 10 years).

● The Agent charged BEPO N100,000 which was said to be for ‘data

capturing’ and also told him he will pay N20,000 to make the collection

faster when the passport is out.

● His capturing date was fixed and he headed to Ibadan on a Tuesday

afternoon, so he could meet up with the time set for capturing which is

Wednesday the following day by 7am at Agodi-gate Passport office,

fixed by Mr Tai, the Agent.

● Bepo Boarded Public Transport when going to Ibadan, a Six-Passenger

Toyota sienna at the Ojota park. The journey lasted for about 50 minutes.

● Ogun, particularly, was benefitting more, of the muted Mikano, a

multi-faceted and there on the Lagos-Ibadan Expin terms These included

industry on the Long Bridge; Multi-Trex at Wawa, which was distressed

due to debt issues; Punch Nigeria Limited and Lifemate Furniture in

Magboro. He saw the signboards of McPherson and Babcock universities.

No wonder, he thought, Ogun prided itself as possibly hosting the highest

number of universities in the country. (Take note of the companies located

in Ogun State).

● Dominion university and First Technical university are located in Oyo

state.

● He loves the sight of the brown roofs, as the Sienna descended the Molete

Over head bridge.

● The legendary poet, J.P. Clark described the city in a poem titled,

'Ibadan'. Bepo struggled to recall some of the lines. Then he asked

Google, which answered him:

Ibadan, running splash of rust

and gold-flung and scattered among

seven hills like broken china in the sun.

● While searching on Google for Clark's poem, his eyes had also caught the

title of a novel -Under the Brown Rusted Roofs, by Abimbola

Adelakun. Bepo hoped to read it later.

● Some Elite areas in Ibadan includes; Ring Road, oluyole, Bodija, and

Akala.

● Bepo proceeded to the Immigration office on Wednesday, when he got

there he was restricted by the immigration officers only to discover that

Tai was not a personnel or staff of the immigration, he just had a business

center close to the immigration. He then proceeded with verifying his

NIN and all, so BEPO proceeded to the Immigration office, after which

he was attended to swiftly, and was told to return for capturing after 3

weeks.

● After the capturing BEPO Tipped the the immigration officer that

attended to him N2,000

(Read this chapter intensively on the Text ,to get full information, This is just a

brief highlight, just major points were picked)

## CHAPTER ELEVEN

## (POINT OF NO RETURN)

● A banner with header “FOR HE GAVE STARDOM HIS VERY BEST”

was made and mounted at the stage of Stardom Schools Main hall for the

farewell ceremony of Mr Adebepo Adewale, The principal.

● The school colour is black and Purple

● In a bid to give the Management time to give him a befitting farewell

ceremony, Bepo called Emirates Airline to shift his flight by a week, he

was asked to pay a fine of $100 which ths school gladly paid.

● The farewell programme began on a Wednesday with a Novelty Match

between the School Team and the staff.

● The game master, Mr Ibe was the Referee, and he made sure the staff won

against the student, the scores of the Match was 3 -2 (this means the staffs

had 3 goals, while the students had 2 goals)

● Stardom School's goalkeeper name was chido, he's a very young goal

stopper.

● Then on Thursday a debate was held in the honour of Bepo , which is

among the laid down activities for the farewell ceremony. The topic of

discussion was “The arts has contributed more to the development of

the country than science”. (Check the Text for more information on the

debate).

● The SS 3 won the debates

● From 1pm to 3pm every Friday, Stardom had socio-cultural activities.

● LACKADAISICAL - (Take note of this spelling)

● Check the Text for more information on the other Activities which was

done during the Farewell programme.

● After the whole activities, The MD, Mrs Ibidun Gloss, in her remarks In

her remarks, expressed deep appreciation to Bepo for contributing what

she called an "unrivalled quota" to the growth of Stardom. According to

her, Bepo was so impactful: if she had her way, she would not let him

leave.

● The MD then invited Mr Bepo to the podium, while all parents, students ,

staff joined hands in the applause, Mr Bepo approached the podium

waving to everyone. "Thank you very much...thank you...thank you..." the

MD said, as the cheers and whistling quietened gradually. Then she

continued: "Perhaps, I need to state this. I am not the one who employed

Mr Bepo. My late father, Chief David Aje, did. He was the one Bepo

met 24 years ago, when he first came to this school. Unlike many others

who faced our interview panels, Bepo only had an encounter with

Dad-that first day. He had submitted his application letter to my father.

They had a chat after Dad had looked through his Curriculum Vitae and

certificates.

"Dad became stuck with him. It was a day in early September of the year.

The arrangement they had was that he would resume on September 14,

as the school returned from its long, end-of-session vacation. There was a

vacancy for English. So, we expected that Bepo would resume the first

day of the session. But he never did, neither the day after nor the third

day - till the end of the week. We were worried and suggested inviting

others who had applied or had been interviewed. But later BEPO arrived

after eights days behind schedule.

(Take Note Mr Bepo, The principal has been working in the school

for 24 years)

● At the end of the programme, The Principal was principal with an

envelope containing a cheque, which was not less than $10,000.

● While wanting to give his remark, he was emotional and was

sobbing, the principal then intervened and everyone clapped for

him.

(Read this chapter intensively on the Text ,to get full information, This is just a

brief highlight, just major points were picked)

## CHAPTER TWELVE

## (...DAWN)

● Bepo was set to leave the country via Emirate Airline at 10pm on

Saturday, he left his house (Adeniyi Jones, ikeja) earlier at 3pm so he

won't miss his flight like he did some years ago when he wanted to visit

his family abroad.

● As Mr Bepo was about stepping out of his house his landlord, Mr

Ogunwale , his wife and their two grandchildren (Jide and Kemi), came

to bid him farewell.

● Before the D-Day, Mr Bepo has sold his Pathfinder sports utility vehicle

for N1.5 Million, Mr Jeremi Amos, stardom School Accountant bought

the vehicle.

● His freezer and other electronics, he gifted it to his landlady.

● On the day he was going, the Landlord, his grandchildren, Mrs Grace

APEH (Vice Principal), also came along with Mr Jeremi Amos

(Accountant) , Mr Oyelana & Mr Audu to Muritala Muhammed

international Airport (MM 2). - (Take note of all the teachers and the

Subjects they teach, check chapter 1 abstract)

● Mr BEPO gifted the landlord grandchildren N5,000

● Check-in started at 5:30pm. After about an hour, going through security

points and getting his bags checked, Bepo got his boarding pass. Seat no

56 - window side - Gate 2A. It was getting late for the Stardom team to

hit the traffic-laden road back home. Almost all lived far from the airport:

Audu, the wag, stayed in Ikorodu, the CRK teacher lived in Mowe, Ogun

State; only the VP and the accountant stayed in by Thay bid Bepo

farewell and departed.

● At 10:45Pm the plane took off.

● During the assembly the second day after the departure of Mr BEPO, the

students really felt the absence of Mr Bepo during the assembly.

● During the assembly, "Don't worry, students. You will soon have another

principal," Mrs Ibidun Gloss assured, as she took the microphone from

the VP. The promise hardly assuaged the students' feelings. A few, who

dared, murmured their non-acceptance of the appeasement. But just as the MD would say more words, a shout of Principoo!" reverberated at the

gate. Was it a joke? All at once, everyone looked in the direction.

There he was! Yes, he!

Bepo, of course, grinning, arms wide open, as the students rushed

towards him, screaming excitedly. They swept him off his feet, bore him

high on their shoulders and began a frenzied dance around the premises.

"I am back! I am back!" he cried. "I am here! I didn't go! I'm not going

again! My heart is here! This is where my heart is! I am here to complete

my mission!"

The man's voice was barely heard as the students gyrated to the school's

victory song:

We're Stars, we're Stars! We're Stars of Stardom!

We're Stars, we're always winning! We're Stars and we have won! No

night so dark! No cloud so mean!

Yet Stardom Schools will win!

That was how Surprising Bepo came back and didn't travel to the

UK anymore, how he came down from the plane and what happened

remained unknown in the Text.

(Read this chapter intensively on the Text ,to get full information, This is just a

brief highlight, just major points were picked)

## THE END…

## CONCLUSION

The aim of this Abstract compilation is to give all prospective candidates a

highlight on the context of this Novel as well as key points to note while

studying and also providing answers to possible questions you might come

across during your Examination. The Novel Text ‘The Lekki Headmaster’ was

written by KABIR ALABI GABAR, it contains twelve (12) Chapters -(Take

note of the numbers of chapters and Full name of the Author)

WARNING: Please do not see this as an alternative to the main text as only key

points are contained in this compiled document, endeavour you read the main

Text, and use this as a supplement/revision tool, Also take note of some

highlighted Words and sentence in each chapter summary. best of luck!.

For questions and clarification you can reach out to me via any of my contact

details below.

2025 Real JAMB Question on LEKKI HEADMASTER as reported by Students

*Questions that came out this morning for the lekki headmaster*

(1) What does chief waliem story teaches us?

(2) In which other business was stardom school involved in?

(3) Who is The man wrongly accused of and got detained for corrupti-

on

(4) What subject did Mr Justus anabel handle in stardom school

(5) What was bepo answer when mrs apeh asked him what is the matter?

(6) The tittle of the king of badagry is?

(7) What are the name of the principal two children

(8) Who is the author of the lekki headmaster?

## *🔥SOLUTIONS TO LEKKI HEADMASTER QUESTIONS*

1. What does Chief Waliem's story teach us? Chief Waliem's story highlights the complexities of corruption and its impact on society. It serves as a cautionary tale about the consequences of unethical behavior and the importance of integrity.

2. In which other business was Stardom School involved? Stardom School was also involved in the hospitality business, operating a guest house alongside its educational services.

3. Who is the man wrongly accused and detained for corruption? Mr. Bepo, the headmaster, was wrongly accused and detained for corruption, highlighting the challenges honest individuals can face within corrupt systems.

4. What subject did Mr. Justus Anabel handle in Stardom School? Mr. Justus Anabel was the Chemistry teacher at Stardom School.

5. What was Bepo's answer when Mrs. Apeh asked him, "What is the matter?" When Mrs. Grace Apeh asked Bepo what was the matter, he did not respond verbally but instead sobbed freely, overwhelmed by emotion.

6. The title of the King of Badagry is? The title of the King of Badagry is "Akran of Badagry."

7. What are the names of the principal's two children? The principal, Mr. Bepo, has two children named Nike and Kike.

8. Who is the author of The Lekki Headmaster? The author of The Lekki Headmaster is Kabir Alabi Garba.
